column1: # pins.tsv — the single statement of which tool versions this repo expects.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS.
# The pins were spread across four places: MODULE.bazel (shellcheck, buildifier,
# via rules_python norminette), tools/requirements.txt, .devcontainer/Dockerfile
# (the apt toolchain) and .bazelrc (which compiler Bazel drives). Nothing stated
# them together, so nothing could check them, and "does this box still match the
# campus?" had no answer short of reading four files by hand.
# tools/env_drift.sh reads this and compares it against whatever the current
# machine actually has. Run on a campus box, it is the whole answer to "have they
# upgraded anything?".
# THREE KINDS OF PIN, and the difference matters.
#   fetched  Bazel downloads it against a sha256 and every layer runs THAT
#            binary, so THIS MACHINE'S copy is not consulted at all -- an apt
#            shellcheck 0.8.0 sitting beside our pinned 0.10.0 is not drift, it
#            is irrelevant. The comparison that means something for these is
#            pin-against-fetch, which is the `fetched-as` column below.
#   campus   The version must MATCH THE CAMPUS BOX, because the Moulinette
#            compiles and runs with it. A mismatch means the suite is testing
#            something other than what the grade comes from -- the failure this
#            whole exercise exists to prevent. These are the ones to re-pin when
#            campus moves.
#   ours     Our own tooling. Nobody's grade depends on it; the only requirement
#            is that everyone gets the SAME one, so it drifts only when we choose
#            to move it. A campus upgrade is irrelevant to these.
# Columns, tab-separated:
#   tool  kind  expected-full-line  version-command  pinned-in  [fetched-as]
# expected-full-line is the WHOLE VERSION LINE the version command printed on
# the machine this was pinned from, suffix and all: the first line carrying a
# dotted version number, or the first non-empty line if none does. Not simply
# the first line -- perl's --version opens with a blank one, which is how the
# audit once recorded it as having no version at all. env_drift.sh and
# env-audit.sh apply that same rule, so a pin and a capture always agree about
# which line they are comparing. It used to be a substring --
# `clang version 12.` -- so that Ubuntu could repackage without reporting drift.
# Right instinct, wrong mechanism: "do not fail on packaging noise" became
# "cannot see the difference at all", and a campus move from 12.0.1 to 12.0.5
# would have gone unnoticed. env_drift.sh now records the full line and GRADES
# the difference instead: major is loud, minor/patch says re-audit, and a
# changed packaging suffix alone is noted and forgiven. Nothing is thrown away.
# fetched-as is optional and names an environment variable holding the path to
# the binary BAZEL DOWNLOADED for this tool, set by //tools:env_drift in
# tools/BUILD.bazel. Where it is present, env_drift compares three things rather
# than two -- the pin, the box, and the fetch -- because once a layer stops
# using the box's binary, "the pin matches the box" no longer implies "the pin
# matches what our checks actually run".
# A VERSION-COMMAND OF `-` means "recorded here, deliberately not probed",
# for a row nothing on the machine can be asked about from here: bazel and
# bazelisk (asking either its version from inside `bazel run //tools:env_drift`
# re-enters Bazel and contends for the lock that very command is holding),
# rust-std-i686 (a library, with no command), and libbsd-dev (the image
# carries two of its manual pages, not the package, so dpkg knows nothing).
# They are still checked, just not from here: //tools:conventions verifies
# that the version this file records is the version the file named in
# `pinned-in` actually installs, which is the drift that can realistically
# happen to them.
# ROWS OBSERVED BUT NOT PINNED: glibc and perl, argued below, and the shell
# piscine's tools, whose own note sits above their rows.
# perl first, because it is the short one. callgrind_annotate is a perl script
# that formats a profile valgrind has ALREADY produced, so the interpreter never
# decides a verdict -- it lays out numbers that exist before it runs. Pinning an
# interpreter to read one text file is the wrong trade. The cycles layers that
# call it SKIP loudly without it (NO_SKIP=1 makes that a failure), and this row
# is here so a campus move is visible all the same.
# glibc is the longer argument.
# It is here because it is the only entry that is not a tool but the RUNTIME
# every deliverable links against, and because nothing was watching it at all.
# It is not fetched, and pinning it would mean shipping a SYSROOT -- headers, the
# shared objects, the crt files and a linker configured to prefer them -- which
# is a different order of work from pointing a runner at a fetched driver.
# The reason that is an acceptable trade, rather than a hole: the allowed-
# function lists across the whole Piscine come to eight libc symbols (write,
# malloc, free, read, open, close, strerror, basename), all POSIX, none of whose
# behaviour has moved in decades. Exactly one of them can produce an observable
# a libc version could change -- strerror's message text ("No such file or
# directory", "Is a directory"), asserted byte for byte in six fixtures of
# c-piscine/c-piscine-c-10/tests: ex01/errmsg.txt and dirmsg.txt, ex02/errmsg.txt
# and dirmsg.txt, ex03/errmsg.txt and allfail.txt. Every case that reads one is
# at strict (the reading of "performs the same function as the system's"
# tool), so a libc or locale that changed the text could move strict verdicts
# only, never basic -- and the locale that decides that text is already fixed
# for every test in .bazelrc. Linking is forward-
# compatible, and unlike the compiler (whose campus copy differs from the
# student's) the harness builds and runs on the same machine, so there is no
# skew to protect against.
# EVERY campus row holds campus's exact string, packaging suffix included. The
# second campus audit (a campus box, 2026-10-13, report 90da4ff6 on
# origin/env-audit-42) checked every one but ld and as under env_drift's own
# rule, and glibc, perl, cc-std and gcc-10-std for the first time: until then
# they had been observed in the DEVCONTAINER only, because the first audit
# (2026-08-09) predates env-audit.sh capturing them. One row differed, glibc:
# it said 2.35-0ubuntu3.13 where campus has 2.35-0ubuntu3.15, and was
# re-pinned on 2026-10-14, because a pin is campus's exact number (the
# owner's ruling). env_drift grades a suffix alone as "repackaged", not drift,
# and --strict ignores it, but on a campus box it prints the re-pin edit as it
# does for drift (since 2026-10-14; it said "Nothing to do" before). ld and
# as are the two rows that report does not capture, so their strings are
# inferred, not observed: they come from binutils-x86-64-linux-gnu, which it
# shows at the pinned 2.38-4ubuntu2.12.
# WHEN CAMPUS MOVES: run `bazel run //tools:env_drift` there, read what it
# reports, and edit BOTH this file and the place named in `pinned-in`. Repinning
# is deliberately manual -- a pin changed automatically is a change to what the
# suite tests, made by nobody.
cc

# ar and ranlib are what a Makefile's recipes run by those names: make_test.sh
# puts the fetched ones first on the recipes' PATH (TO VERIFY V60), with the
# libbfd beside them, which it proves they load. As nm's, each version is the
# frontend's own.
ar
ranlib
# nm's version string comes out of the FRONTEND's own .rodata, so this row
# stays green whichever libbfd the loader supplies -- which it once did while
# the box's 1.5 MB library was doing all the work behind a 44 KB pinned name.
# What actually holds the pin is the --nm-lib flag the three nm-reading
# runners take, and each of them refuses to run unless LD_DEBUG says libbfd
# resolved inside the staged tree. Do not read a green here as that check.
nm
# objdump is nm's sibling from the same package, read by forbidden_symbols.sh
# --function, and the same holds: its frontend prints the version, and what
# holds the pin is --objdump-lib, refused unless libbfd resolved in the tree.
objdump
# ld.bfd links every build the layers make (the cc toolchain's linker), and
# its version, too, is the frontend's; the pin is held by the wrapper
# rl_ld_pin writes (tools/runner_lib.sh), which proves libbfd's directory won.
ld
# as is gcc's assembler, from the same package: the gcc layer's -B points
# gcc at it (defs.bzl's compiler table, `progs`), and env_drift had no row
# for it until conventions read every label a tools/*.bzl pins. As nm's,
# its version is the frontend's own: which libbfd it loads, no row checks.
as
valgrind
perl

column1: # The shell piscine's tools. Every one is the box's own copy: no layer fetches
# them, the shell exercises run on them, and several of the checks do too
# (file, find, tar, git, and ssh-keygen and ifconfig from the openssh and
# net-tools packages these rows stand for). The image installs them
# unversioned (.devcontainer/Dockerfile, "NOT PINNED", says why), so each row
# is observed, not pinned: campus's exact line, from the second campus audit
# (report 90da4ff6, 2026-10-13), which the dev container prints identically.
# ssh's and ip's lines end in another program's version, OpenSSL's and
# libbpf's. env_drift grades a line's first number, the tool's own, as well as
# its last, so a move of either number is drift, and a new Ubuntu revision of
# the same two is a repackaging (on a campus box, that too prints the re-pin
# edit). OpenSSH's portable suffix (8.9p1 to 8.9p2) is not part of its number,
# and reads as a repackaging too.
bash

# llvm-symbolizer turns a sanitizer report's frames into function, file and
# line. It is campus's 12.0.1 build (the llvm-12 .deb beside clang-12's), but
# whether a campus box carries one does not matter: no layer takes it from the
# box, and a sanitizer that found one on PATH would make the same report read
# differently on two machines, so every runner hands over this one
# (tools/runner_lib.sh, rl_sanitizers).
llvm-symbolizer
zig
buildifier
# The Rust toolchain rules_rust fetches, and the i686 core the grader's own
# functions (tools/grader_lib.bzl) are compiled against: rustc loads a core
# only from its own version, so the two are one version, which MODULE.bazel
# writes out (rules_rust's default moves with rules_rust). Neither carries a
# fetched-as: no layer of a student's runs either, and //tools:conventions
# holds MODULE.bazel's two sites to these rows instead. rust-std is a library
# with no command to ask, hence `-`.
rustc
rust-std-i686
bazel
bazelisk
# The strlcpy(3bsd), strlcat(3bsd) and strnstr(3bsd) manual pages, C 02
# ex10's, C 03 ex05's and Libft's contract, and nothing else of the package:
# glibc 2.35 has none of the three functions, so on Ubuntu 22.04 their pages
# ship only here. The image extracts those pages from this .deb and installs
# neither its header nor its library, so no code builds there that would not
# build on a campus box, which need not have them. Whether campus has the
# page is env-audit.sh's to record.
libbsd-dev
